requirements: Run ./gradlew -p ui check with --no-build-cache (or the gate-host equivalent) and record the exact command, exit code, formatting result, JVM and wasm browser test results, fresh XML counts, and logs.

Explicitly report HttpIndexQueryRepositoryTest, IndexQueryViewModelTest, IndexQueryHeaderTest, and ConfigsetsRouteViewModelTest on their applicable runners. Do not count skipped tests as passes; confirm the repository tests compile and run on wasm.
Confirm the request-handler test uses /api/collections/{collection}/config/requestHandlers and parses config.requestHandlers.
Run the invalid-collection test and report that empty, dot, dot-dot, leading-hyphen, slash, query, and percent-encoded path inputs fail before any HTTP request is sent.
Verify a failed handler lookup clears the prior selected handler, leaves the loading state, and displays the error without showing the successful-empty 'No request handlers' message.
Verify a failed collection lookup displays the error without showing the successful-empty 'No collections available' message.

Exercise the Index / Query tab in a running UI connected to a Solr instance with two collections: load collections and handlers, select a handler, switch to a collection exposing the same endpoint and confirm selection is preserved; switch to one without it and confirm selection clears. Record the environment, observations, and evidence; mocked or preview tests are not live integration.
Run root ./gradlew check -x test -Prefguide.include=false and record the result; the ref-guide remains excluded under board policy.

Where practical, adapt the selection-preservation assertion to the old state holder at PR head 90d4efb8486a0ce04ec6a9614b56b8b239b487a0 and show it fails there and passes on this head. If not practical, record why and the coverage limit.

Exercise connection and response decoding failures for collections and handlers: each must reach the error state and leave loading. Verify cancellation propagates when switching collections and does not publish stale results.
In the running UI, select each unfinished Configsets tab and verify it displays the unavailable message; check Overview and Index / Query remain reachable.

Exercise successful responses with missing collections and missing config.requestHandlers fields; both must produce a failure and error state. Confirm explicit empty collections and requestHandlers remain valid empty results and compare these cases with actual Solr responses.

Exercise HTTP 401 and 403 for both collection and handler discovery, a 5xx response, and success. Confirm the authentication message, the correct request-specific access message, generic error, and suppressed empty messages, including recovery when a new collection is selected.

With secured Solr and rule-based authorization, verify an authenticated query-capable user denied collection discovery and a user allowed collection discovery but denied handler configuration, as well as a user allowed both. Record actual policies, status codes, and UI behavior. Check 401 behavior with configured authentication, and assess the existing OAuth refreshTokens TODO separately; do not claim OAuth refresh coverage if not exercised.
